faq: Do I need a discount in a welcome flow?
No. A discount lifts first orders, but many brands do well with a story and a helpful guide instead. We write the version that fits your margins, and you can add an offer at any time.
Will you write the emails in my brand voice?
Yes. Send us your site, a few emails you liked and any words you avoid. We write a draft in your voice, and you can ask for changes within your revisions.
What if I already have a welcome email?
We review it and either improve it or replace it, whichever suits you. We never delete anything until you approve, and we keep the old version saved in your account.
Is SMS allowed in the flow?
Only to numbers that gave clear written consent to receive texts. We build the opt-in step into the signup form and keep the quiet hours and stop-reply rules your region requires.

desc:
A welcome email series for new subscribers introduces your brand at the moment people pay most attention. Ecom Swift LLC writes and builds the series in your own email tool, with copy, layout and timing, and tests it before it goes live.

## What is a welcome flow?

A welcome flow is an automated set of messages that starts when someone joins your list. The first message arrives within minutes and confirms the signup. Later messages tell your story, show your best products, answer common questions and, if you choose, offer a reason to place a first order.

It runs on its own for every new subscriber, so it works at any hour without extra effort from you.

## Why the first days after signup count

A new subscriber has just shown interest. They remember why they signed up, they expect a message and they are likely to open it. A week later that attention fades. If the first thing they receive is a random sale email, the introduction is lost.

A welcome series gives a planned first impression. It sets expectations about what you will send, shows who you are and points to the products and pages that help a new visitor decide. Brands that explain themselves clearly also get fewer questions later. How well it performs depends on your products and audience, but a welcome series is a sensible first automation because every subscriber passes through it.

## What a well-built welcome series includes

- A prompt first message that confirms the signup and delivers anything promised.
- A short brand story that says who you are and what you stand for.
- Best sellers or featured collections, with images and clear buttons.
- Answers to common worries: delivery, returns, sizing and support.
- Customer review blocks, where you already have real reviews to show.
- An optional first-order message, if an offer suits your margins.
- Different paths by signup source or area of interest, where useful.
- A text message for people who opted in to SMS.
- Timing that spaces messages out without flooding the inbox.
- Subject lines that are clear and honest, with alternatives to test.

## How we create it

We start with a short brief on your brand, products and tone, and a look at how people join your list today. Then we write each message, design it with your logo, fonts and colors, and build the flow in your own tool with the right trigger and delays. Existing welcome emails are reviewed, kept or replaced as you prefer.

Basic builds three welcome emails with a signup trigger and timing. Standard builds five emails plus one welcome text, a first-order message, a split by signup source and subject line options. Premium builds seven emails and two texts, with paths by interest, best seller and review blocks, a subject line test on the first email, written notes and a handover call. Add-ons include extra emails, a welcome text and a product quiz email path. Every message is tested on a phone and a computer before the flow is switched on.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Send the first message right after signup.
- Tell new subscribers how often you will write.
- Show real products and real customer photos you have the right to use.
- Make every email easy to act on with one clear button.
- Review the series after a few weeks.

**Avoid:**
- Making the series so long people tire of it.
- Offering a discount you cannot afford.
- Writing only about yourself and not about the reader's needs.
- Sending texts without clear opt-in.
- Leaving an old welcome email running next to the new flow.

## Who it is for

A store with a signup popup but no automated reply is the most common case. A brand relaunching or changing its look can refresh a dated series. A seller adding SMS for the first time can introduce texts inside a flow that people already read.

## What we need from you

Send your store link, tool name, logo, colors, best-selling products and a few sentences about your story. Tell us whether you want an offer. We never need passwords. Access is given as a collaborator, staff or team user where the tool allows it, and you remain the owner of the account.
